label: def:architecture-axis-map
title: Architecture-axis map
body: The compiler architecture uses five disjoint evidence axes. An accepted claim may read evidence from an axis only at the admissible evidence level shown in the displayed axis map; the negative boundary in the last column is part of the claim certificate and cannot be discharged by prose from another axis. \begin{center} \small \begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{p{.16\textwidth}p{.27\textwidth}p{.27\textwidth}X} \toprule Axis & Role in this paper & Admissible evidence & Negative boundary \\ \midrule BEDC source theory & finite-kernel theory, proof obligations, and implementation contracts & pinned source paths, commits, imported labels, bounded summaries, and source-interface records & not a publication acceptance record, not a fresh rebuild, and not a complete BEDC exposition \\ Lean markers & formal-verification records for named obligations & recorded build, axiom-purity, marker-existence, or source-interface rows when named by the package & not object-language closure, not discovery by itself, and not proof of unrelated claims \\ Finite witnesses & manifest/evaluator substrate evidence for artifacts and package certificates & manifest rows, evaluator outcomes, bundled snapshots, verifier logs, file digests, and limitation ledgers & not semantic universality, not whole-tree dynamic validation, and not an unbounded artifact rerun \\ Agents & proposal, search, review, ranking, and repair assistance & advisory drafts, review reports, scheduler scores, and gate-input suggestions after being recorded as such & not proof evidence, not human promotion, not novelty certification, and not gate passage \\ Automath publication compiler & intake, route, overlap, submission-pack, and support surface governance & promotion records, active-paper markers, overlap ledgers, submission-interface maps, digest manifests, command logs, and upload-or-archive records when present & not the whole mathematical contribution, not venue acceptance, and not authority to merge evidence axes \\ \bottomrule \end{tabularx} \end{center}

label: prop:architecture-axis-non-escalation
title: Axis non-escalation
body: In any record-gate-sound package using Definition~\ref{def:architecture-axis-map}, passage or evidence on one architecture axis cannot certify a load-bearing claim whose claim kind requires another axis. More precisely, if a claim certificate uses an axis $A$ but its stronger reading needs an evidence item or negative-boundary discharge listed only on a different axis $A'$, then the stronger reading is not accepted unless the package contains a separate submitted coordinate for $A'$ and the gates assigned to that coordinate pass. Consequently Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} constructs only finite publication certificates whose axis coordinates are explicitly present in the submitted support surface; it does not infer BEDC closure from Lean markers, artifact semantics from manifest rows, proof evidence from agents, venue upload from automath route state, or support-surface availability from local bundle paths.

label: def:operational-acceptance-interface
title: Operational acceptance interface
body: A \emph{claim} is a manuscript assertion that can affect a mathematical, artifact, route, or submission decision. A \emph{load-bearing claim} is a claim whose removal would change a theorem statement, a case-study conclusion, or the submission-readiness status. An \emph{advisory output} is any AI-agent draft, score, suggested theorem, review packet, or repair proposal before a gate records it. A \emph{deterministic gate} is a repeatable predicate, script, or checklist whose inputs and pass/fail decision are recorded independently of the prose generated by an agent. A \emph{human promotion} is the explicit editorial act that moves a candidate into publication state, for example by creating an active \texttt{2026\_*} paper directory with \texttt{main.tex} and \texttt{PIPELINE.md}. An \emph{evidence surface} is the set of source paths, commits, commands, logs, inventories, and witness records cited for a claim. An \emph{acceptance entry} is a manuscript or submission-ledger record that marks a candidate claim as usable in the publication-facing argument. \emph{Accepted work} is the subset of candidate claims with such an entry. This is a status notion only: the definition records that an editorial acceptance entry exists, but it does not by itself assert external editorial acceptance or implementation correctness. A pipeline is \emph{record-gate-sound for acceptance} when each acceptance entry records the claim kind, the evidence surface, the evidence level, and a pass record for every gate in $\Gamma$ assigned to that claim kind, and when a route-boundary entry also records human promotion. The deterministic dispatch function $\Gamma$ from claim kinds to gates is part of the operational interface. Its domain is \[ \{\text{formal-source},\text{ traceability},\text{ route}, \text{ submission},\text{ artifact},\text{ discovery},\text{ work-selection}\}. \] It sends formal-source claims to the build and axiom-purity gates; traceability claims to inventory and marker-existence gates; route claims to promotion, overlap, and submission-state gates; submission claims to submission-pack gates; artifact claims to status and limitation-ledger gates; discovery claims to the pinned discovery gate above and, for extension claims, to the theorem-content delta gate; and work-selection claims to the scheduler gate, whose evidence surface is a critical-path score or backlog window together with the claim kind that the selected item is meant to advance. For mixed claims, $\Gamma$ returns the union of the gate sets for the claim kinds present. The route gates have separate operational meanings. The \emph{promotion gate} uses the active-paper evidence surface, namely a human promotion act producing a \path{2026_*} directory with \path{main.tex} and \path{PIPELINE.md}; passing means the candidate may be daemon-visible publication work, and failing means it remains intake or source material. The \emph{overlap gate} uses route identity, semantic-overlap ledgers, submitted-sibling paths, and program-board state; passing means advancement is route-disjoint or has a recorded resolution, and failing means advancement is blocked until closure, merge, supersession, or waiting for prior feedback. The \emph{submission-state gate} uses submission markers, venue state, board state, and submission-pack metadata; passing means the route's publication state permits the proposed action, and failing means the action would duplicate, race, or under-specify an active or submitted route. The \emph{theorem-content delta gate} uses theorem inventories, hard-lint output, and delta records such as \path{ARTIFACT_INVENTORY.md}; passing means that an extension claim identifies load-bearing mathematical content, and failing means that compilation, file churn, or surface edits may not be reported as substantive theorem growth. A \emph{reviewable artifact} for this paper is either a public repository file, a supplemental file included with the submission, or an explicit historical-evidence boundary stating that the local path is used only as path-verified evidence and not as a fresh command-run claim. A \emph{case witness record} is path-complete when its evidence surface gives a concrete source or artifact path for each load-bearing component of the row. A route-overlap witness has the fields \emph{route identity}, \emph{submitted sibling}, \emph{overlap reason}, \emph{gate decision}, and \emph{allowed next actions}. An artifact-limitation witness has the fields \emph{artifact status path}, \emph{limitation ledger path}, \emph{observed limitation}, \emph{gate decision}, and \emph{allowed manuscript claim}. A promotion witness has the fields \emph{candidate surface}, \emph{human promotion evidence}, \emph{active-paper markers}, \emph{gate decision}, and \emph{allowed manuscript claim}. A theorem-content witness has the fields \emph{changed surface}, \emph{theorem inventory or hard-lint surface}, \emph{substantive-content delta}, \emph{gate decision}, and \emph{allowed manuscript claim}. The inventory files \path{ARTIFACT_INVENTORY.md}, \path{SOURCE_MAP.md}, and \path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json} are part of the evidence surface for this paper and give the compact path catalogue used by Table~\ref{tab:case-witnesses}. We distinguish two evidence levels. A claim is \emph{path-verified} when this paper records the relevant source path, artifact path, pinned commit or local publication path, and gate decision, but does not assert that a command was freshly rerun for this submission. A claim is \emph{command-run} when the paper also records the command, source commit, environment, exit code, and log path for a fresh run. This long technical supplement uses path-verified architecture and case evidence unless explicitly marked command-run. A uniform \emph{pass record} is the finite tuple \[ \rho=(g,I,d,e,\ell), \] where $g$ is the gate name, $I$ is the input surface submitted to that gate, $d$ is the recorded decision, $e$ is the evidence pointer supporting the decision, and $\ell$ is the evidence level. A pass record is assigned to a claim certificate only when its evidence pointer is contained in the claim's evidence surface, in a submitted manifest or table row, in a bundled snapshot, or in an explicit historical-evidence boundary. A \emph{publication certificate} for a load-bearing claim $c$ is the finite record \[ \mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B). \] Here $K$ is the nonempty finite set of claim kinds carried by $c$, $\ell$ is the evidence level, $E$ is the evidence surface, $H$ is either a human-promotion record or the marker that $c$ does not cross the intake-to-publication boundary, $R$ gives one pass record, with the five fields above, for each gate in $\bigcup_{k\in K}\Gamma(k)$, $D$ is present exactly when $K$ contains discovery and then names the pinned discovery-gate source-interface rows used for the claim, and $B$ records either the command-run fields or the explicit boundary that no command-run assertion is made. A certificate is \emph{locally checkable} when these finite fields are present and every path, manifest row, or log named by a field lies in the submitted artifact, the supplemental review bundle, or the explicit path-verified historical boundary. For later use we make the local check explicit as a finite verifier. The concrete package checker supplied with the review bundle is \path{review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py}. Its positive invocation is \path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py}; it reads exactly \path{review_bundle/certificate_schema.json}, \path{review_bundle/current_package_pass_records.json}, \path{review_bundle/submission_interface_map.json}, \path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory.json}, and \path{review_bundle/REVIEW_BUNDLE_MANIFEST.json}, and writes the recorded pass log \path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log}. Its negative-example invocation is \path{python review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py --negative-example review_bundle/negative_certificate_record_example.json}, with recorded log \path{review_bundle/negative_certificate_record_example_run.md}; that fixture upgrades a route row to command-run strength while omitting the command-run tuple and is rejected with the finite bad subrecord \path{neg1: command-run fields incomplete}. The mathematical verifier below is the schema abstraction of this package checker. Let \(\mathsf{Dom}(\Gamma)\) be the seven-kind domain and let \(\mathsf{Lev}=\{\mathsf{path},\mathsf{command}\}\). For a candidate record \(\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\), define six finite predicates: \begin{enumerate} \item[$P_1$:] $K\ne\emptyset$, $K\subseteq\mathsf{Dom}(\Gamma)$, and $\ell\in\mathsf{Lev}$. \item[$P_2$:] $E$ is finite and each item of $E$ is a submitted path, review-bundle path, manifest row, log path, pinned commit, or explicit historical-evidence boundary. \item[$P_3$:] for every gate $g\in\bigcup_{k\in K}\Gamma(k)$, $R$ contains a pass record $(g,I,d,e,\ell')$ whose evidence pointer lies in $E$ or in a named submitted table, manifest row, bundled snapshot, or historical boundary. \item[$P_4$:] $H$ records the human promotion exactly when $c$ crosses the intake-to-publication boundary and otherwise records that no such boundary is crossed. \item[$P_5$:] $D$ is present exactly when discovery lies in $K$, and then names the pinned discovery-gate source-interface rows used by the claim. \item[$P_6$:] $B$ either records command, source commit, environment, exit code, and log path for command-run evidence or explicitly records that no command-run assertion is made. \end{enumerate} Define the finite verifier \[ V(c,\mathcal C)=\bigwedge_{i=1}^{6}P_i(c,\mathcal C,\Gamma). \] If this conjunction is false, the rejected subrecord is the finite set of fields read by the least-indexed failed predicate. This paragraph defines the verifier only; no unprinted semantic oracle is part of it. The next definition packages the same finite fields as an explicit input type and a finite acceptance table; the exactness theorem below then proves that the verifier and the independently named record-acceptance relation coincide on that finite data structure. For a package $P$ with ledger $L$, dispatch table $\Gamma$, and submitted support surface $S$, write \[ \mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma) \] for the following finite predicate. For every acceptance entry of a load-bearing claim $c$ in $L$, there is a publication certificate $\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)$ such that $E\subseteq S$, $V(c,\mathcal C)=1$, each pass record in $R$ is a submitted row of $L$, the row decision is passing, and the row's evidence pointer denotes an element of $S$ at the evidence level recorded in the row. If $B$ does not contain command, source state, environment, exit code, and log path, then $\mathsf{RGS}_{S}$ asserts only this finite row-and-pointer property and asserts no implementation-level correctness of the gate that produced the row.

label: def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface
title: Record-gate soundness external interface
body: The external record-gate interface for a package is the finite predicate \[ \mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma) \] with the following inputs and outputs. Its inputs are exactly a package $P$, a submitted support surface $S$, a finite acceptance ledger $L$, and the deterministic claim-kind dispatch table $\Gamma$ of Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}. Its positive output is the finite family of certificates \[ \{\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B): c\in L \text{ is an accepted load-bearing claim}\} \] such that $E\subseteq S$, $V(c,\mathcal C(c))=1$, every assigned gate in $\bigcup_{k\in K}\Gamma(k)$ has a submitted passing row in $R$, each evidence pointer in such a row denotes an element of $S$ at the recorded evidence level, the human-promotion coordinate $H$ is present exactly at an intake-to-publication crossing, and the discovery and command-boundary coordinates $D$ and $B$ have the presence conditions required by the verifier predicates $P_5$ and $P_6$. Its negative output, when the predicate fails for a ledger row, is only the finite bad subrecord read by the first failed verifier predicate among $P_1,\ldots,P_6$. This interface makes no further claim. In particular it does not assert that an external venue accepted the work, that a command was freshly rerun, that a Lean development builds, that an artifact has the semantic property named in prose, or that an advisory agent output is proof evidence, unless the corresponding source path, command, source state, environment, exit code, log path, or gate row is one of the finite coordinates read above.

label: prop:record-gate-soundness-external-interface-exactness
title: Record-gate interface equivalence and non-claim boundary
body: For the operational acceptance interface of Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}, the standalone interface in Definition~\ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface} is equivalent to the predicate $\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)$ used in the publication-safety theorem. Moreover, under this interface every consequence used by Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} is determined by the finite coordinates $(P,S,L,\Gamma)$ and by the displayed certificates $\mathcal C(c)$; no implementation-level, semantic, venue-acceptance, fresh-execution, or advisory-evidence claim follows from record-gate soundness unless it appears as one of those finite coordinates.

label: def:stronger-reading-preorder
title: Stronger-reading preorder
body: Fix the dispatch table $\Gamma$ and certificate tuple $\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)$ of Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}. A proposed reading $c^{+}$ of the same prose claim is \emph{record-stronger} than $c$, written $c\preceq_{\Gamma} c^{+}$, if at least one of the following finite coordinates is strictly enlarged while the others are unchanged or enlarged: the claim-kind set $K$; the evidence level, from $\mathsf{path}$ to $\mathsf{command}$; the evidence surface $E$; the promotion field $H$; the assigned gate-pass family $R$; the discovery-interface field $D$; or the boundary field $B$. It is \emph{properly stronger} if the enlargement is strict in at least one coordinate. It is \emph{accepted as a stronger reading} only when the enlarged tuple still satisfies $\mathsf{Acc}_{\Gamma}$: every newly added kind has its assigned gates, every newly raised evidence level has the command tuple required by A6, and every new evidence item is on the submitted support surface or in an explicit historical boundary. The preorder is intentionally syntactic and finite-record based. It is not a semantic entailment relation between mathematical propositions, and it does not turn an inventory entry, digest row, or path reference into proof evidence for a theorem-like environment.

label: def:certificate-schema-acceptance-table
title: Certificate-schema acceptance table
body: Fix the seven-kind dispatch table $\Gamma$ of Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}. The verifier input for a load-bearing claim $c$ is the following finite record type: \[ \mathcal C(c)= \{K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B\}. \] Its typed fields are these and only these: $K$ is a finite set of claim kinds; $\ell\in\{\mathsf{path},\mathsf{command}\}$ is the declared evidence level; $E$ is a finite evidence-surface list; $H$ is the route-boundary field; $R$ is a finite family of gate pass records, each with gate name, input surface, decision, evidence pointer, and evidence level; $D$ is either empty or a finite list of pinned discovery source-interface rows; and $B$ is the command-boundary field. This is a data schema, not a theorem: all later exactness claims must be proved from this displayed record and cannot appeal to unlisted package state. Define $\mathsf{Acc}_{\Gamma}(c,\mathcal C)$ to be the conjunction of the six finite table predicates A1--A6 displayed below; no clause may query generated prose, a live daemon, an artifact evaluator, a proof assistant, or a venue state outside these fields and their cited submitted surfaces. \begin{center} \centering \small \begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{p{0.08\linewidth}p{0.22\linewidth}X} \toprule Clause & Field read & Acceptance condition \\ \midrule A1 & $K,\ell$ & $K$ is a nonempty subset of the seven-kind domain and $\ell$ is one of the two evidence levels. \\ A2 & $E$ & Every evidence item is a submitted path, review-bundle path, manifest row, log path, pinned commit, or explicit historical-evidence boundary available at level $\ell$. \\ A3 & $K,R,E$ & For every gate in $\bigcup_{k\in K}\Gamma(k)$, $R$ has a pass record with gate name, input surface, decision, evidence pointer, and evidence level; the pointer lies in $E$ or in a named submitted table, manifest row, bundled snapshot, or historical boundary. \\ A4 & $H$ & $H$ records human promotion exactly when $c$ crosses the intake-to-publication boundary, and otherwise records that no such crossing occurs. \\ A5 & $K,D$ & $D$ is present exactly when discovery lies in $K$, and then names the pinned discovery-gate source-interface rows used by $c$. \\ A6 & $\ell,B$ & $B$ records command, source commit, environment, exit code, and log path for command-run evidence, or records that no command-run assertion is made. \\ \bottomrule \end{tabularx} \end{center}

label: prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier
title: Finite certificate schema verifier as a record check
body: For every load-bearing manuscript claim $c$ whose component kinds lie in the seven-kind domain, $V(c,\mathcal C)$ is a finite, prose-insensitive record-schema verifier for the declared publication certificate. The submitted package instantiates $V$ by the script \path{review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py}. On the positive package input it reads the schema file, pass-record ledger, submission-interface map, primary-claim inventory, and review-bundle manifest named above, and outputs acceptance in \path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log}. On the negative fixture \path{review_bundle/negative_certificate_record_example.json} it outputs rejection in \path{review_bundle/negative_certificate_record_example_run.md} with the bad subrecord \path{neg1: command-run fields incomplete}. If $V$ accepts, then $\mathcal C(c)$ is locally checkable at exactly its declared evidence level. This is certificate-record verification only: it checks finite record shape, dispatch, evidence pointers, and command-boundary discipline, not end-to-end external semantic validation of the referenced artifacts or source theory. If $V$ rejects, then a reviewer can extract a finite bad subrecord consisting of the first failed schema check and the fields on which that check depends.

label: thm:verifier-input-output-contract
title: Verifier input--predicate--output contract
body: The verifier interface used by the publication-safety theorem is exactly the following finite mathematical-software contract. Its input is a pair $(c,\mathcal C(c))$, where $c$ is a load-bearing manuscript claim and \(\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\) is the certificate record of Definition~\ref{def:certificate-schema-acceptance-table}, together with the fixed dispatch table $\Gamma$ and the submitted support surface $S$. Its checked predicates and outputs are: \begin{center} \centering \small \begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{p{0.12\linewidth}p{0.30\linewidth}X} \toprule Check & Predicate actually checked & Possible output \\ \midrule $Q_1$ & $K$ is nonempty, $K\subseteq\mathsf{Dom}(\Gamma)$, and $\ell\in\{\mathsf{path},\mathsf{command}\}$ & accept this coordinate, or reject with bad fields $K,\ell$ \\ $Q_2$ & each item of $E$ is on $S$ or in an explicitly declared pinned, logged, or historical boundary & accept this coordinate, or reject with bad field $E$ and the offending pointer \\ $Q_3$ & every gate assigned by $\Gamma$ to a kind in $K$ has a passing five-field record in $R$ whose pointer is reviewable through $E$, a submitted table, a manifest row, a bundled snapshot, or an historical boundary & accept this coordinate, or reject with bad fields $K,R,E$ and the missing or non-reviewable gate \\ $Q_4$ & $H$ records exactly the human-promotion crossing asserted by $c$, or records that no such crossing is asserted & accept this coordinate, or reject with bad field $H$ \\ $Q_5$ & $D$ is present exactly for discovery-kind claims and then names only pinned source-interface rows used by $c$ & accept this coordinate, or reject with bad fields $K,D$ \\ $Q_6$ & $B$ either contains command, source state, environment, exit code, and log path, or explicitly marks that no command-run assertion is made & accept this coordinate, or reject with bad fields $\ell,B$ \\ \bottomrule \end{tabularx} \end{center} The positive output is only the finite acceptance bit $\mathsf{accept}(c,\mathcal C)$ for these six predicates. The negative output is only the finite bad subrecord belonging to the first failed predicate. In particular, the contract has no output channel for proof-assistant validity, daemon correctness, artifact semantics, fresh case-study reruns, venue upload, or venue acceptance. Therefore any theorem in this paper that invokes the verifier can certify exactly finite record acceptance for the submitted schema and cannot certify end-to-end workflow correctness unless an enlarged input schema and an additional proved verifier contract are supplied.

label: thm:record-acceptance-exactness
title: Schema-relative finite-record acceptance exactness
body: Fix the seven-kind dispatch table $\Gamma$, the two evidence levels, and the typed certificate tuple $\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)$ of Definition~\ref{def:certificate-schema-acceptance-table}. For every load-bearing claim $c$ and every finite candidate certificate $\mathcal C(c)$, the finite verifier $V$ of Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface} and Theorem~\ref{thm:verifier-input-output-contract} accepts $\mathcal C(c)$ if and only if the six-clause table predicate $\mathsf{Acc}_{\Gamma}(c,\mathcal C)$ holds. This is a schema-relative and finite-record-relative assertion: both sides read exactly the fields named in the fixed schema and in the finite submitted record surface, and neither side ranges over unrecorded semantic facts about the referenced mathematics, artifacts, or gate implementations. Moreover, if $V$ accepts a record for $c$, the same record cannot certify any stronger reading $c^{+}$ that adds a new claim kind, a stronger evidence level, an omitted route crossing, an omitted discovery interface, an omitted pass record, or a command-run assertion: such a reading has a finite bad subrecord of the corresponding clause. Thus $V$ is exact for this paper's finite record-acceptance relation over the submitted source, tables, manifests, logs, and explicitly declared historical boundaries, while remaining silent about external semantic validity of the referenced theory or artifacts and about the implementation-level soundness of any deployed gate implementation beyond the recorded pass rows.

label: cor:executable-schema-exactness-negative-fixture
title: Executable schema exactness and negative fixture
body: Under the hypotheses and fixed schema of Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}, the executable verifier instance \path{review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py} is a finite witness of the same schema-relative relation, not an additional semantic oracle. On the positive submitted package it can witness exactly the records satisfying \(\mathsf{Acc}_{\Gamma}\) at their declared evidence levels. On the negative fixture \path{review_bundle/negative_certificate_record_example.json}, which upgrades a route record to command-run strength while omitting the command, source state, environment, exit code, and log path, the extracted bad subrecord is exactly the evidence-level declaration together with the incomplete boundary field. Hence the executable example separates the verifier contract from any stronger reading: changing prose or ambient pipeline state while keeping the finite schema fields fixed cannot change either the acceptance bit or the first failed finite subrecord.

label: thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary
title: Finite-coordinate determination and trust-boundary classifier
body: Fix the dispatch table $\Gamma$ and the verifier $V$. Let $F_{\Gamma}$ be the finite schema projection read by $V$ from a certificate record, namely the claim-kind set, declared evidence level, evidence surface, promotion field, gate-pass rows, discovery-source rows, command-boundary tuple, and the assigned gate set determined by $\Gamma$. If two ambient pipeline or artifact states induce the same values of all coordinates in $F_{\Gamma}$ for a claim $c$, then they induce the same record-acceptance decision and the same finite publication certificate for $c$. Therefore the exactness of Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness} is exactness only relative to this finite schema projection. No property depending on a coordinate outside $F_{\Gamma}$---for example the semantic truth of a referenced theorem, truthful production or implementation soundness of a gate row, a fresh Lean build result, a daemon trace, an artifact semantic fact, a theorem-environment completeness claim, or an external venue decision---is a consequence of the accepted certificate unless that property is first encoded as an additional finite certificate coordinate and the enlarged record is accepted. In particular, record-gate soundness is a load-bearing hypothesis for Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}; it is not supplied by schema exactness alone.

label: prop:machine-readable-certificate-records
title: Machine-readable certificate records
body: For the current presentation package, the finite record checker $V$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier}, with the record-acceptance semantics of Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}, has an executable record-level instance over the review bundle, conditional on exact supplemental inclusion of \path{review_bundle/} in the completed submission with matching final digests, as stated in Proposition~\ref{audit:review-bundle-availability-condition}. The schema file \path{review_bundle/certificate_schema.json}, the pass-record ledger \path{review_bundle/current_package_pass_records.json}, the primary-interface map \path{review_bundle/submission_interface_map.json}, the primary-claim inventory \path{review_bundle/primary_claim_inventory.json}, the verifier script \path{review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py}, and the recorded run \path{review_bundle/certificate_verification_run.log} instantiate the verifier at the declared evidence levels for entries $a_1,\ldots,a_7$. The negative fixture \path{review_bundle/negative_certificate_record_example.json} and recorded run \path{review_bundle/negative_certificate_record_example_run.md} instantiate the first failure mode for a forbidden command-run escalation. Each pass record in the ledger has the five fields \emph{gate name}, \emph{input surface}, \emph{decision}, \emph{evidence pointer}, and \emph{evidence level}. The machine-readable submission-interface map is locked to rows \path{sim1}--\path{sim4} of Table~\ref{tab:submission-interface-map} by its row identifiers, certificates, surfaces, and evidence levels; the primary-claim inventory is locked to rows \path{pc1}--\path{pc12} by its row identifiers, source locations, row classes, and evidence levels. These executable locks check the finite record interface; full semantic equality between prose paraphrases and mathematical meaning, soundness of the gate implementations, and path completeness beyond the declared surfaces remain outside the record-check claim and stay at the manual audit boundary stated in the row classes.

label: thm:executable-record-non-escalation
title: Executable record non-escalation
body: Let $F$ be the finite field projection read by \path{review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py}: manifest-field presence, entries $a_1$--$a_6$, claim-kind membership, evidence-level membership, assigned-gate coverage, pass-record fields, evidence-level agreement, discovery-field discipline, path-verified boundary status, row locks for \path{sim1}--\path{sim4}, and row-class locks for \path{pc1}--\path{pc12}. Assuming the exact-or-archive-equivalent review-bundle support surface of Proposition~\ref{audit:review-bundle-availability-condition}, among all assertions about the current review bundle that are functions only of this projection, Proposition~\ref{prop:machine-readable-certificate-records} proves the maximal executable claim: the six current-package certificates satisfy the finite record-acceptance relation of Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness} at the declared path-verified fields under the input--predicate--output contract of Theorem~\ref{thm:verifier-input-output-contract}, and no accepted row carries a command-run boundary. Thus the bundled Python script is an implementation witness for the finite schema, not a separately formalized verifier-language semantics. In particular, the executable verifier cannot certify any strictly stronger assertion whose truth depends on prose-to-semantics equality, independent extraction of claims from the manuscript, completeness of paths not declared in the records, or the external semantics of a Lean development, publication daemon, artifact suite, evaluator, or venue state.

label: thm:executable-certificate-construction-invariant
title: Executable certificate-construction invariant
body: For the submitted review bundle, let $G$ be the union of the finite fields read by the two executable verifiers \path{review_bundle/verify_source_interface_record.py} and \path{review_bundle/verify_certificate_records.py}. Thus $G$ contains the ten source-interface table triples, the JSON source-interface records, the pinned source snapshot path, digest, line count, declared source commit and line ranges, the six current-package pass-record entries $a_1,\ldots,a_6$, the submission-map rows \path{sim1}--\path{sim4}, the primary-inventory row locks \path{pc1}--\path{pc12}, and the two recorded successful verifier logs. On the equivalence class of packages with the same projection $G$, the publication-safety interface has a unique executable finite certificate construction: the imported discovery-gate interface is the sixteen-row checked source interface of Proposition~\ref{prop:source-interface-record-file-consistency}, the accepted current-package certificates are exactly the six records of Proposition~\ref{prop:machine-readable-certificate-records}, and any stronger reading that changes the source interface, adds an accepted row, raises the evidence level, adds a command-run assertion, or asserts external semantic or venue correctness is not determined by $G$ and is rejected at the finite-record boundary unless new certificate fields and verifier records are supplied. This is a finite-record construction invariant: the scripts witness the listed predicate checks on bundled JSON and table fields, and no claim is made here that Python itself has been given a separate formal operational semantics.

label: prop:claim-kind-dispatch
title: Deterministic claim-kind dispatch
body: For every load-bearing manuscript claim whose kind lies in the seven-kind domain above, $\Gamma$ assigns a unique finite set of deterministic gates. In a pipeline that is record-gate-sound for acceptance, a mixed load-bearing claim may be used as accepted work only if its acceptance entry records passage through every gate in the union assigned to its component kinds.

label: thm:mixed-claim-projection-obstruction
title: Mixed-claim projection obstruction
body: Let $c$ be a load-bearing mixed claim with nonempty component-kind set $K\subseteq\mathsf{Dom}(\Gamma)$ and submitted candidate certificate $\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)$. For a nonempty subset $J\subseteq K$, write \[ G_J=\bigcup_{k\in J}\Gamma(k) \] and let $c_J$ denote the projected reading of $c$ that keeps exactly the claim-kind components in $J$ and keeps the same declared evidence level, evidence surface, promotion boundary, and command boundary, except that the discovery field is required precisely when discovery lies in $J$. Then the following are equivalent for the projected reading $c_J$: \begin{enumerate} \item the finite verifier accepts the projected certificate $\mathcal C_J=(J,\ell,E,H,R|_{G_J},D_J,B)$, where $R|_{G_J}$ is the restriction of $R$ to rows whose gate name lies in $G_J$ and $D_J$ is $D$ exactly when discovery lies in $J$ and is absent otherwise; \item every gate $g\in G_J$ has in $R$ a pass record with the five required fields and with an allowed evidence pointer, the retained boundary fields $E$, $H$, $D_J$, and $B$ satisfy the corresponding schema clauses at level $\ell$, and $J\subseteq\mathsf{Dom}(\Gamma)$. \end{enumerate} Consequently, if an acceptance entry for $c$ records passage only through a proper gate subset $Q\subset\bigcup_{k\in K}\Gamma(k)$, then every component subset $J$ with $\neg(G_J\subseteq Q)$ has an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord, namely a missing pass record for some gate in $G_J\setminus Q$. In particular, no passage through route, submission, scheduler, artifact, traceability, formal-source, or discovery gates can certify a mixed claim's remaining component unless the pass rows assigned to that remaining component are also present.

label: thm:assigned-gate-soundness-audit-boundary
title: Assigned-gate soundness audit boundary
body: Let $P$ be a finite submitted package with pass-record ledger $L$, dispatch table $\Gamma$, and submitted support surface $S$. For a load-bearing claim $c$, write $G(c)=\bigcup_{k\in K(c)}\Gamma(k)$ for the finite set of gates assigned to its claim-kind set. The package may use a ledger row for $c$ as a sound record-gate witness only through the finite predicate $\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)$ of Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}. Equivalently, the available finite-record strength is exactly the following: \begin{enumerate} \item for every $g\in G(c)$ the submitted ledger contains a pass row for $g$, including the gate name, input surface, decision, evidence pointer, and evidence level; \item every evidence pointer named by those pass rows denotes a submitted path, manifest row, theorem/proposition/table label, uploaded bundle file, or explicitly declared historical boundary at the evidence level stated in the row; and \item if the manuscript asserts any stronger proposition that the underlying gate implementation was independently sound, freshly executed, or semantically correct beyond the recorded finite schema check, the submitted package also contains a gate-soundness audit tuple for that stronger proposition: source path, command, source state, environment, exit code, and log path for the assigned gate. \end{enumerate} Consequently, in the absence of the audit tuple in (3), record-gate soundness is an explicit hypothesis of the publication-safety theorem, not a theorem proved by the current package. The finite pass rows prove only the package-level statement that no accepted ledger claim omits an assigned gate row or its declared submitted evidence surface.

label: thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton
title: Finite certificate obstruction skeleton
body: Let $c$ be a load-bearing manuscript claim whose component kinds lie in the seven-kind domain. The verifier of Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier} gives the following complete audit classification at the declared evidence level. A certificate for $c$ passes the publication-safety interface if and only if it has no bad subrecord of the following five types: \begin{enumerate} \item missing evidence surface for the declared evidence level; \item missing pass record for a gate in $\bigcup_{k\in K}\Gamma(k)$; \item missing human-promotion record when the claim crosses from intake or source material into active publication work; \item discovery escalation without the pinned discovery-gate source-interface rows for certificate, ledger, lineage, and boundary witnesses; or \item command-run escalation without command, source commit, environment, exit code, and log path. \end{enumerate} Equivalently, every unsafe accepted claim contains an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord of one of these five types, and deleting all other fields preserves the same rejection by the verifier. This is an audit-skeleton theorem for the software-workshop route: it classifies finite certificate failures and makes no claim about theorem-proving complexity or about fresh execution of the underlying workflow.

label: thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form
title: Finite extension-budget normal form
body: Fix the dispatch table $\Gamma$, the finite certificate schema, and an accepted finite certificate \(\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\) for a load-bearing package claim $c$. Let $c^{+}$ be a proposed stronger reading of the same row which is not record-equivalent to $c$ in the sense of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-coordinate-determination-boundary}. Then $c^{+}$ is accepted by the publication-safety interface if and only if the submitted finite record surface contains an extension record in the following normal form: \[ \Delta(c,c^{+})=(\Delta K,\Delta E,\Delta H,\Delta R,\Delta D,\Delta B), \] where the nonempty coordinates are exactly the coordinates needed by the stronger reading: \begin{enumerate} \item $\Delta K$ names every additional claim-kind component asserted by $c^{+}$; \item $\Delta E$ supplies the submitted evidence surfaces for those added components at the declared evidence level; \item $\Delta R$ supplies pass records for every gate in \(\bigcup_{k\in K\cup\Delta K}\Gamma(k)\) not already supplied by $R$; \item $\Delta H$ supplies any newly asserted promotion, route, venue, or external instantiation boundary; \item $\Delta D$ supplies the pinned discovery-source rows whenever the stronger reading adds discovery, classifier-shift, or theorem-content-delta content; and \item $\Delta B$ supplies the command, source-state, environment, exit-code, and log-path tuple whenever the stronger reading raises a path-verified row to command-run strength. \end{enumerate} Equivalently, every genuine strengthening has positive finite extension budget: at least one coordinate of \(\Delta(c,c^{+})\) must be nonempty, and every nonempty obstruction class from Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton} must be paid by the corresponding coordinate of \(\Delta(c,c^{+})\). Without this extension record, the stronger reading has an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord and remains outside the certificate constructed in Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}.

label: prop:gate-interface-separation
title: Gate-interface separation
body: The promotion, overlap, submission-state, and theorem-content delta gates are separate deterministic interfaces. None can be replaced by passage of another one when a load-bearing claim has the corresponding component.

label: cor:human-promotion-daemon-active-track-separation
title: Human promotion is not daemon-visible active-track equivalence
body: In the operational interface of Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}, a human-promotion record and daemon-visible active-paper markers are not interchangeable certificate fields. More precisely, let $c$ be any route-boundary claim whose accepted certificate is $\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)$. The certificate may be read as saying that a candidate is admitted to the publication-facing package only when the promotion field $H$ records the human editorial act and the corresponding route-gate pass record in $R$ names the active-paper marker surface required by the promotion gate. A record containing only a human-promotion note but no active-paper marker surface does not certify daemon visibility, and a record containing only a daemon-visible \path{2026_*} marker surface but no human-promotion field does not certify editorial promotion. In particular, the intake-isolation row $a_3$ of Tables~\ref{tab:current-acceptance-ledger} and~\ref{tab:current-certificate-ledger} supports exactly the bounded lesson that the intake packet remains outside daemon-visible publication work until both sides of the promotion interface are recorded; it does not identify human promotion with daemon enumeration.

label: prop:scheduler-selection-advisory
title: Scheduler selection is advisory before discovery gating
body: Let $s$ be a scheduler or critical-path score attached to a candidate claim $c$. If $s$ recommends selecting $c$, then the recommendation is a work-selection claim and by itself can only pass the scheduler gate. If $c$ is also asserted to be a discovery or classifier-shifting contribution in a record-gate-sound pipeline, then the accepted mixed claim must pass both the scheduler gate and the discovery gate. Consequently, critical-path scores may prioritize review order, and the imported classifier-shift selection rule may break ties among otherwise equal discovery potential coordinates, but neither score nor recommendation accepts a classifier-shift discovery unless the discovery gate also supplies the required certificate, ledger, and lineage witnesses.

label: prop:publication-safety-minimal-bad-record-witness
title: Minimal bad-record witness for command-run escalation
body: In the operational interface of Definition~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface}, let $r$ be a submitted claim record whose claim-kind set is \{route\}, whose evidence level is declared to be command-run, and whose boundary field contains no command-run tuple $(\text{command},\text{source state},\text{environment},\text{exit code}, \text{log path})$. Suppose all other route coordinates of $r$ are filled: there is an evidence pointer, a human-promotion marker at the declared boundary, and pass rows for the promotion, overlap, and submission-state gates. Then the schema verifier rejects $r$, and the inclusion-minimal bad subrecord is exactly the pair consisting of the evidence-level declaration ``command-run'' and the boundary field missing the five command-run coordinates. In particular, adding more prose, advisory scores, route history, or path-verified evidence surfaces cannot repair the rejected stronger reading unless the missing command-run tuple is added as a finite coordinate.

label: thm:publication-safety-interface
title: Conditional finite-record safety interface under record-gate soundness
body: Consider a theory-to-paper pipeline with the operational interface above and a finite submitted record surface consisting only of the manuscript source, printed tables, submitted manifests, uploaded review-bundle records, recorded logs, and explicitly declared historical boundaries. Assume the following four distinct finite-record hypotheses. \begin{enumerate} \item \emph{Acceptance entries}: every load-bearing claim in an active manuscript is either rejected or has an acceptance entry with an evidence surface inside this finite submitted record surface. \item \emph{Record-gate soundness}: writing $S$ for this finite submitted record surface and $L$ for the acceptance ledger, the package satisfies the finite predicate $\mathsf{RGS}_{S}(P,L,\Gamma)$ of Definitions~\ref{def:operational-acceptance-interface} and \ref{def:record-gate-soundness-external-interface} as proved equivalent in Proposition~\ref{prop:record-gate-soundness-external-interface-exactness} and as delimited by Theorem~\ref{thm:assigned-gate-soundness-audit-boundary}: every recorded acceptance entry has the assigned passing rows and submitted evidence pointers, every advisory output is demoted unless the deterministic gate set $\Gamma$ for its claim kind passes, and no independent implementation-soundness, fresh-execution, or semantic-correctness claim about the gates is inferred unless the package also contains the corresponding source path, command, source state, environment, exit code, and log path. \item \emph{Discovery certificate input}: discovery claims are checked through the pinned discovery-gate interface certified by Lemma~\ref{lem:source-interface-extraction-correctness} and Propositions~\ref{prop:reviewable-source-snapshot-interface}, \ref{prop:source-interface-record-file-consistency}, and \ref{prop:source-interface-evidence-level-separation}, in particular the separated manual/path-verified and executable finite-record levels for the pipeline safety and main pipeline theorem labels. \item \emph{Promotion and verifier boundary}: no inactive intake seed is treated as publication work without human promotion, and the constructed tuple below is submitted to the finite schema verifier rather than being identified with the acceptance entry itself. \end{enumerate} Then, and only under these finite-record hypotheses, the package checker has the following finite-record invariant. The checker input is the submitted surface $S$, the ledger $L$, the dispatch table $\Gamma$, and the schema files and bundle records named in Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier}. Its output is the finite accepted set \[ \mathsf{Out}_{\Gamma,S}(L)= \{(c,\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)):\ V(c,\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c))=1\} \] together with the finite list of rejected bad subrecords. For every accepted load-bearing claim $c$ it constructs, from the acceptance entry and the submitted finite evidence surfaces, a record \[ \mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)=\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B) \] accepted by the finite schema verifier of Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier} with the input--predicate--output boundary of Theorem~\ref{thm:verifier-input-output-contract}; equivalently, by the schema-relative finite-record exactness of Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness}, the constructed record satisfies the schema-relative record-acceptance semantics for the dispatch table $\Gamma$. Consequently, within the submitted finite records and under the stated explicit record-gate-soundness hypothesis, $c$ has a recorded evidence surface, a declared evidence boundary, and a prior pass record for every gate required for its claim kind. Accepted discovery claims additionally inherit the bounded pinned source-interface consequences that statement-only, code-only, mechanical-expansion, and compression-only outputs are not accepted as discovery without the required certificate, ledger, and lineage witnesses. Moreover, the constructed record is axis-and-level invariant and sharp for the stronger-reading preorder: if $c\preceq_{\Gamma}c^{+}$ is a properly stronger reading that moves a load-bearing consequence from one architecture axis of Definition~\ref{def:architecture-axis-map} to another, raises the evidence level from path-verified to command-run strength, adds an implementation, artifact, venue, or semantic-correctness assertion, or adds a theorem-obligation completeness assertion, then $c^{+}$ is accepted by the same interface if and only if the submitted record surface contains the corresponding finite extension coordinates and those records pass the assigned gates. If those coordinates are absent, the accepted certificate is maximal below $c^{+}$: it still accepts $c$ and rejects the stronger reading by a finite bad subrecord. The maximality of this constructed certificate is stated separately in Proposition~\ref{prop:publication-safety-maximality}, and the exact finite price of any genuine strengthening is classified by Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}; the current-package instantiation is stated separately in Corollary~\ref{cor:publication-safety-current-package-instance} and refined by Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness}.

label: thm:finite-record-certificate-rigidity
title: Finite-record certificate rigidity
body: Fix the finite submitted record surface $S$, acceptance ledger $L$, dispatch table $\Gamma$, and schema verifier $V$ used in Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}. Assume the same record-gate soundness and source-interface hypotheses as that theorem. For every accepted load-bearing claim $c$ with certificate \(\mathcal C(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)\), the following are equivalent for a properly stronger reading $c^{+}$ in the preorder of Definition~\ref{def:stronger-reading-preorder}. \begin{enumerate} \item The same interface accepts $c^{+}$ over $S$. \item The submitted surface contains exactly the finite extension coordinates required by the normal form of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form} for the changed axis, evidence level, discovery component, artifact-semantic component, implementation-soundness component, theorem-completeness component, command-run component, support-surface component, or venue component, and those added coordinates pass the gates assigned by $\Gamma$. \end{enumerate} If these coordinates are absent, $c$ remains accepted but $c^{+}$ is rejected by an inclusion-minimal bad subrecord of one of the types classified in Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}. Consequently the publication-safety theorem is a finite-record certificate invariant under record-gate soundness: it is invariant under changes to unsubmitted implementations, Lean states, daemons, artifact reruns, venue states, archive locators, and source checkouts that leave the finite tuple \((K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B),S,L,\Gamma)\) unchanged, and it certifies no stronger fact than that tuple records.

label: thm:boundary-axis-non-escalation-exactness
title: Boundary-axis exact non-escalation
body: Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, and let \(c\) be any load-bearing claim accepted by the finite certificate constructed there. The following five stronger readings of \(c\), when they are not already record-equivalent to \(c\), are accepted by the same publication-safety interface if and only if the submitted finite support surface contains the indicated positive extension coordinates and the added coordinates pass the gates assigned by \(\Gamma\): \begin{enumerate} \item An \emph{external implementation-soundness reading} is accepted exactly when the package adds implementation-soundness records for the relevant external gate: the implemented gate or checker identity, its source state or version, the specification it is asserted to implement, and either a pass row for the implementation-soundness gate or a command-run tuple with command, source state, environment, exit code, and log path. \item An \emph{exact source-theorem import reading} is accepted exactly when the package adds an exact source-statement or formal-rebuild coordinate: the pinned source path and commit, the exact statement text or formal object being imported, and a checked exact-statement appendix, Lean/BEDC rebuild record, or equivalent command-run record whose pass rows are part of the submitted surface. \item A \emph{semantic source-validation reading of the source-interface record comparison} is accepted exactly when, in addition to table/JSON/snapshot consistency, the package adds the semantic source-validation coordinate from the previous item for the source theorem whose truth is being used. \item An \emph{artifact-semantic reading of a finite-witness row} is accepted exactly when the package adds the evaluator contract or artifact-semantic pass row for the asserted Rule110/GroundCompiler property, or a fresh evaluator command-run tuple tied by manifest row to the submitted artifact. \item A \emph{theorem-environment completeness reading of a theorem-obligation ledger} is accepted exactly when the package adds a deterministic theorem extractor coordinate: extractor identity and source state, the source files it scans, the extraction command, environment, exit code, log path, and the equality or inclusion certificate relating the extractor output to the submitted theorem inventory. \end{enumerate} If the corresponding positive coordinates are absent, the original claim \(c\) may still be accepted at its declared finite-record level, but the stronger reading is rejected by an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord. Hence the main safety interface, the manual source-interface extraction lemma, the executable source-interface comparison, the finite-witness manifest theorem, and the submitted theorem-obligation ledger theorem are jointly rigid: none can be used to derive implementation soundness, exact source-theorem truth, semantic source validation, dynamic artifact semantics, or theorem-environment completeness without paying the matching finite extension budget.

label: prop:certificate-constructor-bad-subrecord-extractor
title: Certificate constructor and bad-subrecord extractor
body: Assume the four finite-record hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}. For every ledger row \(c\) there is a deterministic partial constructor \[ \mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B) \] and a deterministic extractor \(\mathsf{Bad}_{\Gamma}(c)\) with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item \(\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)\) is defined and accepted if and only if the six-clause predicate \(\mathsf{Acc}_{\Gamma}(c,\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c))\) holds. \item If \(\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)\) is rejected, then \(\mathsf{Bad}_{\Gamma}(c)\) is an inclusion-minimal finite bad subrecord of one of the five obstruction skeletons in Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}: missing submitted evidence, missing assigned gate record, missing route or external decision field, missing pinned discovery row, or unsupported command-run boundary. \item For every properly stronger reading \(c^{+}\) of an accepted row, the same extractor rejects \(c^{+}\) exactly at the first unpaid positive extension coordinate of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-extension-budget-normal-form}; if no such coordinate is added, \(c^{+}\) is not distinct from \(c\) in the finite-record preorder. \end{enumerate} Consequently the publication-safety theorem has both a positive certificate construction algorithm and a negative bad-subrecord extraction algorithm, each bounded by the submitted schema fields.

label: prop:publication-safety-maximality
title: Finite-record maximality
body: Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface}, the constructed certificate is maximal with respect to the finite submitted record surface. More precisely, let $c$ be an accepted load-bearing claim and let $\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)=(K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B)$ be the certificate constructed in that theorem. If a stronger reading $c^{+}$ asserts any external end-to-end compiler correctness, current execution of unrecorded gates, proof-assistant correctness, current formal-source currency, dynamic artifact semantics, or venue acceptance, then either $c^{+}$ is not a distinct finite-record consequence of $\mathsf{Cert}_{\Gamma}(c)$, or its certificate must strictly enlarge one of $K,\ell,E,H,R,D,B$ by adding the corresponding claim kind, evidence surface, gate pass record, promotion or venue field, discovery-interface row, or command-run tuple. In the latter case, if the enlargement is absent, a finite bad subrecord is returned by Theorem~\ref{thm:record-acceptance-exactness} or by one of the obstruction types of Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}.

label: cor:publication-safety-current-package-instance
title: Current-package source-level instance of the safety interface
body: For the current package, assume the support-surface condition later closed by Theorem~\ref{thm:final-support-surface-closure}: the exact supplemental \path{review_bundle/} directory is uploaded with the submission, or an archive-equivalent replacement with matching final digest records is supplied. Under that explicit availability condition, the finite pass-row components of the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} are witnessed by the machine-readable evidence map of Proposition~\ref{prop:machine-readable-certificate-records}, the acceptance ledger of Proposition~\ref{prop:current-package-acceptance-certificate-ledger}, the assigned-gate boundary of Theorem~\ref{thm:assigned-gate-soundness-audit-boundary}, and the four path-complete case witnesses of Proposition~\ref{prop:path-complete-case-witnesses}. Therefore the current package instantiates the construction theorem as a certificate-construction and certificate-checking result for the finite records actually supplied, with the bounded schema-relative package certificate exactness isolated in Theorem~\ref{thm:current-package-certificate-exactness}.

label: cor:finite-record-gate-soundness-boundary

label: thm:implementation-soundness-extension-criterion
title: Exact extension criterion for implementation-soundness readings
body: Fix the dispatch table $\Gamma$ and the finite certificate schema of Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-certificate-schema-verifier}. A reading of a load-bearing package claim as an implementation-soundness claim is accepted by the same publication-safety interface if and only if the submitted finite record surface is enlarged by an implementation-soundness extension record \[ \mathsf{Impl}(c)=(K^{\mathrm{impl}},E^{\mathrm{impl}},R^{\mathrm{impl}},B^{\mathrm{impl}}) \] with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item $K^{\mathrm{impl}}$ contains the additional implementation claim kind or claim-kind component being asserted, rather than merely reusing the original finite-record claim kind of $c$. \item $E^{\mathrm{impl}}$ is a submitted finite evidence surface naming the implementation object being certified: for example the relevant source path, version or commit, configuration, executable verifier, and implementation-log surface. \item $R^{\mathrm{impl}}$ contains a pass record, with evidence pointer inside $E^{\mathrm{impl}}$, for every gate assigned by $\Gamma$ to the enlarged claim kind $K\cup K^{\mathrm{impl}}$. \item $B^{\mathrm{impl}}$ declares the evidence level of the implementation claim and contains the command-run tuple whenever the implementation claim is asserted at command-run strength. \end{enumerate} When such an extension record is present, the finite certificate constructor of Theorem~\ref{thm:publication-safety-interface} accepts the enlarged claim exactly at the evidence level declared by $B^{\mathrm{impl}}$. When it is absent, every implementation-soundness reading of the same row has a finite obstruction of one of the five kinds in Theorem~\ref{thm:finite-certificate-obstruction-skeleton}. The current package supplies no record of the displayed form $\mathsf{Impl}(c)$ for the package verifiers or gates. Thus the theorem is a future-facing exact criterion rather than an implementation-soundness result for this submission: it says precisely what finite record must be added before a later package may make that stronger claim.
